ordered_diagnoses: Eosinophilic dermatitis due to other causes

facts.raw_span: A woman in her 70s with recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
presented with a pruritic rash ongoing for 2 weeks
The rash started as an erythematous papule on her right arm 2 months after initiation of a new immunotherapy regimen
then gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
She denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
A recent trial of oral terbinafine yielded no improvement
Erythematous annular plaques without scale on her right arm and bilateral legs
4-mm punch biopsy from right arm showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils
Periodic acid–Schiff (PAS) stain was negative for fungal organisms
Hematoxylin and eosin stain demonstrating superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation
Hematoxylin and eosin stain demonstrating numerous scattered eosinophils

concepts.why: The biopsy findings of eosinophilic dermatitis could be due to other causes, and the temporal relationship with immunotherapy is not the only possible explanation.

The presence of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils, as well as the negative PAS stain for fungal organisms, points to eosinophilic cellulitis as a possible diagnosis.

rationales.F02: Pembrolizumab is a known cause of eosinophilic dermatitis.
rationales.F04: The temporal relationship between immunotherapy initiation and rash onset suggests a possible association.
rationales.F07: The lack of response to terbinafine makes a fungal infection less likely.
rationales.F09: The presence of numerous eosinophils is a hallmark of eosinophilic dermatitis.
rationales.F12: The presence of numerous eosinophils is a key feature of eosinophilic dermatitis.
